newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-HAESSLER TO STAY AT KARLSRUHE FOR NEXT THREE SEASONS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HAESSLER TO STAY AT KARLSRUHE FOR NEXT THREE SEASONS.

text.p: German international Thomas Haessler ended months of speculation about his future on Saturday when he announced he would be staying at German first division side Karlsruhe for the next three seasons.
The diminutive midfielder, who is recovering from a broken leg, has been linked with Bayer Leverkusen and his former club Cologne in the past few months.
Karlsruhe's board were so concerned about the talk that they told Haessler earlier this week to make up his mind by Monday whether he was staying or going.
Haessler, capped 83 times for his country, hopes to sign a contract this week which will keep him at the club until the end of the 1999/2000 season.
"This is a very important signal for the team," Karlsruhe general manager Klaus Fuchs said. "We are delighted that he has decided to stay. There was speculation that the whole team would fall apart."

Despite their success in Europe in recent seasons Karlsruhe are not one of Germany's more glamorous clubs. They would have suffered by losing Haessler, especially as South African-born striker Sean Dundee is also wanted by several top clubs.

The 30-year-old Haessler, who enjoyed a successful time in Italy with Juventus and Roma before returning to Germany in 1994, recently underwent an operation on his broken left leg and is not expected to be fit for another four weeks.
